question: Does the candidate Q108 core preserve Q97's 30-second warning persistence, and can a separate wrapper reproduce it without changing hard stops?
observation: Q108 evaluate_sample reports warning on the first threshold-crossing sample; Q97 calibrated policy requires 30 consecutive 1-second samples. This affects warning cadence, not hard-stop decisions.
testPlan: Moderate PSI samples 1-29: no warning; sample 30: warning.
Recovery below warning threshold resets the consecutive-sample counter.
Severe PSI hard stop remains at sample 15, independent of warning cadence.
ASTRA 1M high-RSS control with healthy PSI remains continue/no-warning.
Missing telemetry continues to fail closed through the unchanged Q108 parser/core.
implementation: Create a Q110-only candidate wrapper over the unchanged Q108 core; do not alter production or Q108 artifacts.
gates: Run only the CPU synthetic policy regression; no model inference or memory allocation.
